lines.text: Desert and savanna on the edge of the Sahara, crossed by caravans and a great river. This is the story of Niger, from Agadez to today.
Around 1430 Tuareg sultans made Agadez their seat, a desert trading town that later raised a great mud-brick minaret.
Along the Niger River, the Songhai built the largest West African empire of its time, rich from trade across the Sahara.
Centuries later the French conquered the land. In 1916 Hamani Diori was born, who would become the first president.
In 1952 came Mahamadou Issoufou, who would lead the country from 2011 to 2021.
In 1954 W National Park was created on a bend of the Niger, savanna shared with Benin and Burkina Faso.
In 1960 Niger became independent from France, a vast country that is mostly Sahara.
A year later Abdourahamane Tchiani was born, the general who would seize power in 2023.
Uranium became Niger's great treasure, and the French company now called Orano mined it for half a century.
In July 2023 soldiers removed President Mohamed Bazoum, the latest of several coups since independence.
Later that year Niger joined Mali and Burkina Faso in the Alliance of Sahel States, turning away from France.
Between the Sahara and the river, Niger is still writing its own path.
